answer: Coordination Harbor Pricing. Each identity gets a fixed daily quota of distinct counterparties it may contact; exceeding it requires a nebula ticket—a signed, publicly logged permit whose price doubles for every prior permit the same identity buys in that period. Tickets are valid only within one forge of shared counterparties, so rings can't pool them. An attacker running N sybils must buy roughly N² tickets to reach real users, making each fake identity cost superlinear in tickets and log exposure.
